problem: Calculate the points where the ellipse $4(x-3)^{2}+9{y}^{2}=72$ intercepts the $x$-axis.
worked_solution:
To calculate the $x$-intercept, we need to substitute $y=0$ into the equation of the ellipse and solve the resulting equation for $x.$ Doing this, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}4(x-3)^{2}+9{y}^{2} & =72 \\ 4(x-3)^{2}+9\cdot {0}^{2} & =72 \\ 4(x-3)^{2} & =72 \\ (x-3)^{2} & =18 \\ (x-3) & =\pm \sqrt{18} \\ (x-3) & =\pm 3\sqrt{2} \\ x & =3\pm 3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the ellipse intercepts the $x$-axis at $(3-3\sqrt{2},0)$ and $(3+3\sqrt{2},0).$
